stories.title: Evaluation of the feasibility of classifying various upper limb movements using multichannel upper-arm sEMG signals
stories.description: Surface electromyography (sEMG)-based upper limb movement recognition studies have primarily focused on signals measured from the forearm or muscles around the wrist. However, the feasibility of using upper-arm sEMG signals as an alternative measurement site for classifying various upper limb movements remains insufficiently investigated. This study evaluated the feasibility of classifying eight upper limb movements, including elbow, forearm, wrist, and hand movements, using five-channel upper-arm sEMG signals. sEMG signals were collected from the biceps brachii long head, biceps brachii short head, triceps brachii long head, triceps brachii lateral head, and brachialis in seven healthy adult males under static and free conditions. Time-domain features were extracted, and classification performance was compared using Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, and k-Nearest Neighbors models. Random Forest achieved the highest accuracies of 93.13 ± 0.70% under the static condition and 89.16 ± 1.21% under the free condition. The full feature set and five-channel configuration showed high performance, although lower recall and increased misclassification were observed for hand open and hand close movements under the free condition. These findings provide preliminary evidence for the feasibility of within-subject upper limb movement classification using upper-arm sEMG signals and suggest their potential as a complementary measurement site.

stories.title: Retrieval practice reshapes neighboring memories in a naturalistic continuous-recognition dataset
stories.description: Retrieval can facilitate or impair related memories, but most evidence comes from laboratory paradigms with experimenter-defined relationships. Here, we asked whether retrieval-related associations emerge in temporal neighborhoods of a large naturalistic continuous-recognition dataset. We analyzed 72,402 target tests from the Natural Scenes Dataset and modeled target recognition as a function of prior tests of neighboring images. Closest-neighbor analyses showed a local dissociation: accurate same-session neighbor retrieval predicted better target recognition, whereas accurate across-session neighbors and inaccurate same-session neighbors predicted poorer target recognition. Accumulated weighted-history models showed broader positive associations for accurate retrieval history and negative associations for inaccurate same-session history. These findings suggest that retrieval-related spillover in naturalistic memory depends jointly on retrieval success, session context, and neighborhood scale.

stories.title: Impact of a multi-component exercise program on circadian protein regulation and sleep quality in healthy females: a randomized controlled trial
stories.description: Among the various clock genes, Cryptochromes have been identified as pivotal constituents of the molecular clock regulating the circadian rhythm. Evidence suggests that physical activity exerts an impact on both the circadian rhythm and the sleep quality. In this regard, this study aimed to assess the effects of multi-component exercise program (MCEP) on circadian protein regulation and sleep quality in healthy and non-active females. A total of twenty-two untrained young women (18–40 yrs), were randomly assigned to two parallel groups: exercise (EXE; n = 11; BMI = 22.23 ± 2.19 kg/m2; Age = 26.09 ± 4.88 years) and control (CON; n = 11; BMI = 23.57 ± 2.79 kg/m2, Age = 29.09 ± 6.3 years) using simple randomization. Outcome assessors were blinded to group allocation. The EXE group implemented a (MCEP) consisting of moderate-intensity aerobic exercises, resistance exercises, and balance exercises for 3 consecutive days. The study was conducted over 4 days and 3 nights by measuring Cryptochrome1 protein (CRY1), sleep quality, blood pressure, heart rate, and body temperature at 08:00, 00:00, and 18:00. This study was conducted at the sports complex and guesthouse of the Faculty of Physical Education at Allameh Tabataba’i University. Results showed there was no significant relationship between the CRY1 levels and Sleep quality (r= -0.36, p = 0.123). Moreover, (MCEP) had no significant effect on the serum level of CRY1 (p = 0.144). Overall, in other measurements, a significant difference was observed in heart rate (HR) within the EXE group (p = 0.001, effect size = 0.27 (0.3% decreased)), and in systolic blood pressure (SBP) within the CON group (p = 0.001, effect size = 1(9% increased)). Conversely, there is a significant decrease in diastolic blood pressure (DBP) in the EXE group when compared to the CON group (p = 0.009, effect size = 0.91). However, in the sleep quality index, the subjective sleep quality in the EXE group significantly increased (p = 0.039, effect size = 0.55 (122% increased)), and sleep latency showed a significant decrease in the CON group (p = 0.021, effect size = 0.55 (50% decrease)). In this study, aerobic training (AT) was conducted at up to 60–70% of HRmax for 30 min, while resistance training (RT) lasted 20 min. Future research could extend (AT) duration to 40 min or adjust the intensity (e.g., 65–75%), incorporate other equipment (e.g., weight) in (RT) with increased repetitions and sets, and extend the overall exercise duration to 90 min. Additionally, future studies should focus on long-term adherence to optimize benefits. The trial was registered with the Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (IRCT) under registration number [IRCT20260722070304N1]. The trial record is available at [https://en.irct.ir/trial/92016].

stories.title: DODGEN Reports POE Devolatilization Milestones Across Three Industrial Projects in China
stories.description: SHANGHAI, Oct. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- DODGEN supplied devolatilization technology to three Chinese polyolefin elastomer (POE) projects in 2026: two successfully started up at CNPC Daqing Petrochemical and Xingchuan New Materials, while Shaanxi Yuneng signed a supply contract with DODGEN. The projects highlight the role of devolatilization in plant start-up, product consistency and operating performance.

stories.title: Atom Processor Observes Unpredicted Slowdown in 2D Quantum Magnet Dynamics
stories.description: Pasqal's 256-qubit neutral-atom processor observed an unexpected slowdown in a 2D quantum magnet's dynamics, diverging from classical simulations. This research, detailed in a preprint, explores the relaxation landscape of a 2D transverse-field Ising model, uncovering three distinct physical behaviors including a previously unpredicted relaxation slowdown at intermediate field strengths. The study highlights the quantum processor's ability to explore non-equilibrium condensed-matter regimes beyond the limits of classical tensor-network simulations.

stories.title: UK Space Agency and DSIT Publish Quantum Technology Roadmap for Space Targeting 2035-2040 Sovereign Capabilities
stories.description: The UK Space Agency and DSIT have published a Quantum Technology Roadmap for Space, outlining strategic priorities for 2035–2040. The roadmap identifies four investment themes: assured timing, resilient sensing, sovereign communications, and long-term computing, aiming to transition prototypes into flight-qualified space systems. It also emphasizes the need to address engineering bottlenecks and proposes immediate actions to strengthen the UK's sovereign industrial capabilities in quantum space technology.

stories.title: Google DeepMind unveils Genie 4: Why Sundar Pichai calls it ‘our most realistic and interactive world model'
stories.description: Google DeepMind announced Genie 4, a new AI world model that creates realistic, interactive simulations in real time with physics and native audio.
